_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-standalone terraria/tmodloader/egg-t-modloader.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence). Octail changes the install script (the release from the GitHub API checked against the SHA-256 digest GitHub lists, the optional GitHub login really sent (upstream's alias never applied in a script), a version that doesn't exist fails instead of silently installing the latest, failures exit non-zero) and adds the terraria and tmodloader tags, generic TCP idle sleep (off until staff enable it per server), a broadcast command, install sandbox defaults and resource hints.
name: tModloader
author: parker@parkervcp.com
description: tModLoader is essentially a mod that provides a way to load your own mods without having to work directly with Terraria's source code itself. This means you can easily make mods that are compatible with other people's mods, save yourself the trouble of having to decompile and recompile Terraria.exe, and escape from having to understand all of the obscure "intricacies" of Terraria's source code. It is made to work for Terraria 1.3+.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Vanilla tModloader Installation Script (pelican-eggs, changed for Octail: the release from the GitHub API, checked
# against the SHA-256 digest GitHub lists for it, the GitHub login actually sent when set, failures exit non-zero)
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail
## install packages to get version and download links
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq curl jq unzip file ca-certificates > /dev/null

AUTH=()
if [ -z "${GITHUB_USER:-}" ] && [ -z "${GITHUB_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "using anon api call"
else
    echo "user and oauth token set"
    AUTH=(-u "${GITHUB_USER:-}:${GITHUB_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}")
fi

## get release info and download links: latest, or a tag such as v2025.12.3.0 (v0.11.8.9 and older: the legacy builds)
VERSION="${VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
    API="https://api.github.com/repos/tModLoader/tModLoader/releases/latest"
else
    API="https://api.github.com/repos/tModLoader/tModLoader/releases/tags/${VERSION}"
fi
if ! RELEASE=$(curl -fsSL "${AUTH[@]}" "$API"); then
    echo "Installation failed: tModLoader release ${VERSION} wasn't found on GitHub."
    exit 1
fi
TAG=$(echo "$RELEASE" | jq -r '.tag_name')
if [[ "$TAG" == v0* ]]; then
    ASSET=$(echo "$RELEASE" | jq -c '[.assets[] | select((.name | test("linux"; "i")) and (.name | test("\\.(zip|tar\\.gz)$"; "i")))][0] // empty')
else
    ASSET=$(echo "$RELEASE" | jq -c '[.assets[] | select(.name | test("^tmodloader\\.zip$"; "i"))][0] // empty')
fi
if [ -z "$ASSET" ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: release ${TAG} has no server download."
    exit 1
fi
NAME=$(echo "$ASSET" | jq -r '.name')
DOWNLOAD_LINK=$(echo "$ASSET" | jq -r '.browser_download_url')
DIGEST=$(echo "$ASSET" | jq -r '.digest // empty')

## mkdir and cd to /mnt/server/
mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

## download release
echo "Downloading ${NAME} (${TAG})"
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$NAME" "$DOWNLOAD_LINK"
if [ -n "$DIGEST" ]; then
    if ! echo "${DIGEST#sha256:}  ${NAME}" | sha256sum -c --quiet -; then
        rm -f "$NAME"
        echo "Installation failed: the download doesn't match its checksum."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    echo "GitHub lists no checksum for this release; not checked."
fi

FILETYPE=$(file -F ',' "$NAME" | cut -d',' -f2 | cut -d' ' -f2)
if [ "$FILETYPE" == "gzip" ]; then
    tar xzf "$NAME"
elif [ "$FILETYPE" == "Zip" ]; then
    unzip -q -o "$NAME"
else
    rm -f "$NAME"
    echo "Installation failed: ${NAME} is neither a zip nor a tar.gz."
    exit 1
fi

if [[ "$TAG" == v0* ]]; then
    chmod +x tModLoaderServer.bin.x86_64
    chmod +x tModLoaderServer
else
    if [ ! -f tModLoader.dll ]; then
        echo "Installation failed: tModLoader.dll is missing after unpacking ${NAME}."
        exit 1
    fi
    #tiny startup script for backward compatibility
    echo 'dotnet tModLoader.dll -server "$@"' > tModLoaderServer
    chmod +x tModLoaderServer
fi

echo "Cleaning up extra files."
rm -rf terraria-server-*.zip "$NAME"
if [[ "$TAG" != v0* ]]; then
    rm -rf DedicatedServerUtils LaunchUtils PlatformVariantLibs tModPorter RecentGitHubCommits.txt ./*.bat ./*.sh
fi

## using config for difficulty as the startup parameter does not work -> config parser
if [ -f /mnt/server/serverconfig.txt ]; then
    sed -i 's/^#difficulty/difficulty/' /mnt/server/serverconfig.txt
fi
grep -q '^difficulty=' /mnt/server/serverconfig.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 'difficulty=0' >> /mnt/server/serverconfig.txt
mkdir -p /mnt/server/saves/Worlds /mnt/server/mods

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: tModLoader ${TAG}."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: World Name
variables.description: The name for the world file.

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: The maximum number of players a server will hold.

variables.name: tModloader Version
variables.description: latest, or a release tag from https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/releases such as v2026.08.3.0. Players need the same version. Reinstall to switch.

variables.name: GitHub User
variables.description:
GitHub user to use for api calls.

This only needs to be set if you hit the GitHub API too often across multiple servers.

variables.name: GitHub OAuth Token
variables.description:
This can be either an OAuth or a Personal Access Token.

This is required for the install is you set a user.

variables.name: Difficulty
variables.description: Sets the difficulty of the world when using auto-create. Options: 0(normal), 1(expert), 2(master), 3(journey)

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description:
Server password for users to connect to your server.
Can be empty for no password.

variables.name: MOTD
variables.description: Message of the Day for the server
variables.default_value: Please don’t cut the purple trees!
